highlights.title: Michigan Residents Voted to Get Corporate Money Out of Politics. Now Utilities Are Suing
highlights.summary: Amid rising electricity costs, Michiganders decisively voted for a ballot proposition to curtail the ability of utilities to spend on elections—a move utilities say limits their freedom of speech.
body: Michigan residents overwhelmingly passed a ballot measure last week intended to restrict the ability of utilities and state contractors to influence politics. Now, the utilities are fighting back.
In a lawsuit filed last Thursday, the two major utilities in Michigan, Consumers Energy and DTE, argue that the measure—dubbed Proposal 2—threatens their First and 14th Amendment rights.

The ballot measure, which passed with 81 percent of the vote, amends the state’s campaign finance laws to put restrictions on donations for both utilities and companies with more than $250,000 annually in state and local government contracts. The new language explicitly bans political donations from utilities, contractors, and high-level employees, lobbyists, and their immediate family members. The ballot measure also tightens the state’s regulations around disclosures for political ads, mailers, and other forms of communication.

highlights.title: ChatGPT Plus for veterans and servicemembers
highlights.summary: More than 20,000 veterans and transitioning service members have claimed a free year of ChatGPT Plus. See how they use it to prepare for civilian careers.
body: In the past year, more than 20,000 transitioning servicemembers and veterans have claimed a year of ChatGPT Plus at no cost after being offered free access by OpenAI. As Veterans Day approaches, that milestone gives us a chance to look at how veterans are using AI to prepare for civilian careers and to figure out what comes next for themselves and their families.

The effort started with veterans who work here at OpenAI, people who use these tools every day and know firsthand how challenging the transition can be. Beyond the free access, OpenAI Academy and our community partners have hosted more than a dozen trainings for nearly 1,000 members of the military community, with seven more ⁠ (opens in a new window) scheduled before the year ends.

Leaving the military often means stepping into an unfamiliar job market and working out how years of service translate into a civilian role. Many veterans are turning to ChatGPT to organize their job search, rehearse for interviews, and explore paths they hadn’t considered.

highlights.summary: Luke Littler says he thought he would be facing pub players on his recent Netflix show, which was billed as giving "amateurs a chance at life-changing money".
body: Broadcast live globally on the streaming platform last month, the cash was won by top women's player Fallon Sherrock.
The format of 'Beat Luke Littler' saw 24 players selected to take on the world number one in a single leg of 501, hoping to win a prize of £501,000.
The 24-strong field did include low-level opponents, such as an Australian jockey, a bin man and a Nando's manager, but anyone who was not a member of the PDC Tour was also allowed to compete.

That meant Sherrock - who became the first female player to beat a male opponent at the PDC World Championship on her way to the last 32 in December 2019 - and leading junior players Mitchell Lawrie and Zach Griffiths were also eligible.

highlights.title: Magic's Best Unofficial Format Is So Big, Burger King Is Running a Tournament
highlights.summary: If you think that the Universe Beyond crossover with beloved sci-fi franchise Star Trek is the biggest thing currently going on in the Magic: The Gathering world, think again. On Nov.
body: Announced through Burger King's Italian website, "Burger King Quest: The Great Gathering" will run from Nov. 10 to Nov. 30. Hungry fans can buy a Great Gathering Bundle at any Burger King restaurant for 19.90 euros ($22.20). The bundle includes a menu, choosing between Double Cheese King, Chicken Krispper, and Whopper Plant Based, plus a deck box and 100 sleeves branded with Burger King x Magic graphics. The deck box in particular has sent Magic players into a frenzy, and it's allegedly already sold out, with scalpers selling it online for ridiculous prices.

This is only half of what Burger King and Magic are cooking, pun intended. Also starting on Nov. 10, nine Burger King restaurants throughout Italy will host Magic tournaments. The winners will qualify for a big final showdown held during the Milan Games Week & Cartoomics, on Nov. 27-29. The tournaments will use the Pauper format, an unofficial 60-card constructed format that allows use of almost every card printed at the common rarity throughout the history of Magic.

body: The founding team behind Top Drives and F1 Clash developer Hutch has raised $5m to build a new company focused on interactive generative video.
Anorak’s pre-seed round was co-led by Play Ventures and Backed VC, with Supercell and MTG also taking part. Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron is among the angel investors.

The startup is led by CEO Shaun Rutland, who co-founded Hutch before MTG acquired it for $375m in 2020, and chief creative officer Jonathan Alpine, who held the same role at Hutch. David Amor is COO, and cofounder Tak Fung runs the company’s AI lab in Chengdu, China. Anorak now has a team of 20 across London and Chengdu.
As we reported last week, Rutland has been teasing Anorak through his blog, describing it as a studio focused on “interactive generative video”.

highlights.title: Give Me the Ball! review – tennis trailblazer Billie Jean King is ferocious force for equality
highlights.summary: Sparky and engaging documentary about the ‘battle of the sexes’ player, who fought her whole career to ensure the women’s game got the respect it deserved. After the engaging Evert and Navratilova documentary Chris and Martina: The Final Set comes this watchable and engaging documentary portrait of…
body: King (née Moffitt) was a ferocious force in women’s tennis from the 60s onwards and a vehement but polite advocate for equal rights on prize money. The women’s game was equally skilful, though not possessed of the same brutal brawn-power, and sold as many stadium seats. King sensationally helped to launch the Virginia Slims women’s tour – one of the great commercial revolutions in US sports, and had to work hard on promotion and sponsorship at the same time as simply training and playing. And while all this was happening, she had to come to terms with her gay sexuality, while married to the poignantly devoted Larry King, who is a gallantly supportive interviewee here.

In the 80s, King was put through another ordeal when her vengeful ex-partner Marilyn Barnett sued for “galimony”, thus revealing King’s sexuality to the world, which again she had to face out at a press conference in the company of her husband and bewildered parents. This is an enjoyable film, though I was surprised that no male tennis player could be found to praise King’s importance, not even the otherwise ubiquitous John McEnroe.

highlights.title: A 13-Year-Old Asked AI About Suicide on Her School Laptop. It Didn’t Get Flagged for Weeks
highlights.summary: The young girl’s parents allege that she used Gemini via her school Chromebook to plan her suicide, but the school’s monitoring systems didn’t know until it was almost too late.
body: A 13-year-old girl spent three months using her school-issued laptop to discuss depression, research suicide, and plan her funeral before self-harm-monitoring software finally prompted school officials to alert her parents, who intervened and stopped her, according to a lawsuit filed this month by her parents.

The lawsuit alleges that Google and parent company Alphabet were negligent in their rollout of a Gemini model, claiming that the AI chatbot “coached” the North Carolina teenager to consider taking her own life. The case, which was previously reported by The New York Times, is one of several that allege harm from AI chatbot use, including claims of delusions and suicide. But it also illustrates the limitations of surveillance tools that thousands of schools have adopted in recent years, which are ostensibly designed to protect students from themselves when browsing and chatting online.

highlights.title: League One clubs aim for further curbs on spending as budgets continue to spiral
highlights.summary: Wage bills in third tier have increased by 15% this season. ‘Luxury tax’ and three-year limits on losses considered. League One clubs want to introduce new spending restrictions to reduce losses by limiting investment from owners.
body: Clubs in the division voted to tighten the rules last summer by reducing spending limits from 60% to 50% of turnover, and removed a staggered approach to owner investment, so that only 50% of equity injections can be spent on squad costs, with the rest assigned to infrastructure projects. Less than six months later many want to go further.

The Guardian has learned that two proposed models are being considered: a cap on the amount clubs can lose over three years, and the introduction of a luxury tax by which 50% of owner investment above a capped threshold would be redistributed to their rivals – with the former proposal seen as the favoured outcome.

The move to introduce more spending curbs comes despite a legal challenge to the existing rules from the Professional Footballers’ Association, which launched proceedings in August on the grounds that the clubs had failed to abide by the terms of their membership of the professional negotiating and consultative committee.
An attempt by League One and League Two to introduce salary caps of £2.5m and £1.5m respectively was withdrawn in 2021 after the PFA took them to an independent arbitration panel.

highlights.title: ‘Apart’ Star Luca Pasqualino and Creator Stelana Kliris Unpack a Love Story Amid War and Apartheid
highlights.summary: The film, starring Leem Lubany and inspired by the experiences of the writer-director's parents who emigrated from Cyprus to South Africa, opens Tallinn's Critics' Picks program.
body: Apart will get its world premiere at the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia on Friday, Nov. 13, opening its Critics’ Picks section.

“In 1974, when Turkey invades Cyprus, young Eleni (Lubany) leaves her homeland through an arranged marriage and finds herself in Apartheid South Africa, swapping one divided country for another,” teases a synopsis for the film. “There, a new life with Nico (Pasqualino) slowly turns into love, until an unexpected friendship forces her to confront a secret from her past.”

Kliris wrote and directed Apart and produced it with Susan Simnett, Jamie Harvey and Ioanna Bolomyti. The cinematographer is Simon Sarketzis, with Emilios Avraam handling editing. Reinvent Yellow Sales is handling sales. Watch a trailer for Apart right here.

Pasqualino, who is now back on Disney+ in the second part of season 2 of the hit show Rivals, and Kliris talked to THR about Apart, how it was shot in Cyprus and captures a 1970s aesthetic, casting challenges, and how urgent the themes explored in the film feel.

highlights.title: Touch of evil: the terrifying truth about sleep paralysis
highlights.summary: One in five people have experienced this frightening state – and the Harvard neuroscientist Baland Jalal has dedicated his career to studying it. Could it be a portal to a deeper understanding of the mind?
body: The Harvard neuroscientist Baland Jalal is considering the unfathomable depths of the human brain. “It can contemplate itself, and vast galaxies, spirits, souls, poetry, Einstein. Yet you hold it in your hand and it seems so trivial.” Jalal’s passion – the subject that drove him to become a scientist – is sleep paralysis, a brain glitch that can fill its host with terror so palpable that it can cause lasting trauma. “What you get very close to in sleep paralysis,” he says, “is that subjective world of the mind. It’s very hard to put into words.”

He should know – he’s spent 271 pages trying to do so. His new book, The Phantom Mind, argues that by exploring the borderlands of sleep, where sleep paralysis occurs, we can delve deeper into how all aspects of our minds work. He may wear a lab coat and examine brain regions and neurochemicals, but studying the mechanics, he says, doesn’t damp down the mysteries of consciousness. “For me, actually, I’ve become more spiritual and interested in the world of mystery and, I want to say supernatural, but dimensions that are intangible, by studying something like sleep paralysis.”

highlights.title: A New Benchmark for De-Aging Comes From Slowly Turning Back Cells’ Clocks
highlights.summary: Researchers in Germany gradually reversed human cells’ ages by decades. By doing so, they could track the de-aging process in a way previous rejuvenation experiments could not.
body: Scientists have long known how to make cells younger—at least in the sense that adult cells can be converted into pluripotent stem cells very similar to those found in embryos. While this capability has been foundational for biological research, these methods aren’t viable for anti-aging technologies, for a few reasons.
“You don't want to have a pluripotent cell in your body, because it can become all types of cells,” says Oliver Brüstle, a professor who studies stem cells at Germany’s Bonn University.

Additionally, the few key genes involved in the stem cell conversion process can drive the formation of cancer if left active. That’s why Brüstle and his team have looked for other ways of de-aging cells without going through a pluripotent state. In their recent study published in Aging Cell, the researchers started with blood cells from people of various ages, including an infant and a 101-year-old donor.
points: Researchers in Germany gradually reversed human cells’ ages by decades.
By doing so, they could track the de-aging process in a way previous rejuvenation experiments could not.

highlights.title: Nvidia’s crisis has corporate governance experts reaching for the popcorn
highlights.summary: The governance experts we talked to say nobody has seen anything like what's unfolding right now.
body: Nvidia’s stock sank 5.47% on Tuesday, following a 4% drop on Monday, a loss of about 9.5% in two days, even though there wasn’t much news out of the company. CEO Jensen Huang has reportedly been trying to conduct business as usual after admitting to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies believe was spying for China. The biggest development: the board hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct an internal investigation.

What comes next is mostly a guessing game, even for the people who study how boards are supposed to handle crises. Two corporate governance professors, Ann Lipton of the University of Colorado and Todd Henderson of the University of Chicago, say there is no real precedent for a CEO caught up in a suspected honeypot. And while they have views on what the investigation should ask, like everyone else, they’re watching to see how it plays out.

highlights.title: Liverpool incorrectly denied pen vs Arsenal says independent panel
highlights.summary: Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty when Jurrien Timber pulled Alexander Isak's shirt in Arsenal's victory at Anfield, an independent panel has ruled.
body: The Key Match Incidents (KMI) panel assesses refereeing incidents across every Premier League match and voted 4:1 that referee Andy Madley should have awarded Liverpool a spot kick.
The panel also voted 3:2 that VAR Stuart Attwell should have intervened and sent Madley to the pitchside monitor on the basis that it was a clear and obvious error.

Arsenal led 1-0 through Kai Havertz's goal, which proved to be the winner, when Isak attempted to head Bradley Barcola's cross in the 21st minute on November 1, but was pulled back by defender Timber.

One KMI panellist believed "the short-lived holding to lack clear impact on the ability of Isak to progress", while two panellists argued, "the subjectivity in assessing impact meant this did not meet the high threshold for VAR intervention".

highlights.title: Monster Hunter Wilds' upcoming Ascendance expansion may be getting a beta, some curious Steam backend updates suggest
highlights.summary: Monster Hunter Wilds 's first expansion, Ascendance, is set for release sometime next year. But, judging by some very suspect recent changes to the Wilds beta app on Steam, we may be playing some of the new stuff earlier than we thought.
body: On Steam, Capcom quietly updated the Monster Hunter Wilds Beta app to now say Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance Beta test. You can see the change log on SteamDB (via PC Gamer ), which also shows an updated key art - all signs that point towards an impending beta for Ascendance.

Seeing as Ascendance itself doesn't have a release date, beyond a nebulous 2027 target, it's hard to speculate when Capcom plans to release the beta. Sometime early in 2027 would be a good guess, perhaps alongside a release date announcement.

Capcom has shown off Ascendance on multiple occasions, more recently in Sony's September State of Play, where we got to see a number of the expansion's new features. A few days later at Tokyo Game Show, we got a first look at returning Elder Dragon Teostra, which we can hunt in the expansion.

Capcom is keen for Ascendance to deliver the level of challenge Monster Hunter is known for, following feedback that the launch version of Wilds simply lacked that expected level of difficulty. While post-launch updates have certainly raised the level of challenge, Ascendance looks to be the next step up.

highlights.title: Sali Hughes on beauty: a lotion to cure autumn dryness – and relieve eczema sufferers’ sore skin
highlights.summary: Bioderma’s new eczema lotion will be comforting for anyone with dry skin. Plus another brilliant problem solving mosituriser. I spent much of my childhood basted in crude, heavy-duty emollient creams and grim bath oils.
body: Although unctuous emollients are necessary to protect a compromised skin barrier, they have a habit of just “sitting” there greasily, refusing to sink in or curtail the itch. The French pharmaceutical brand Bioderma is finally advancing the conversation. Its extensive research into eczema, as well as a recent study of 500 sufferers (about one in five children and one in 10 adults struggle with the condition), were presented as a breakthrough in eczema care at last month’s EADV (European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology) conference in Vienna.

Bioderma believes that eczema-compromised skin does not crave mere generic emollients, but lacks a precise combination of 15 lipids. The brand has sought to replace them with a new product, Atoderm AD Intensive Baume (£26), which is patented and approved for use on babies too. Trial results showed the “balm” (misnomer – it’s a thick lotion) soothed itching from the first second of application, and reduced the urge to scratch by 88%.
points: Bioderma’s new eczema lotion will be comforting for anyone with dry skin.

highlights.summary: World of Warcraft: Forever is a time vampire. Since its release last Wednesday, I have spent 78 hours in Azeroth. Some of that I was AFK, sure. But for many of those hours, I was lost, happily, in the rolling hills and vast planes of Blizzard's MMO - now enhanced, beautified, and given a new social…
body: The original World of Warcraft is so beloved, so influential, that I wasn't convinced Forever could build upon it without cheapening the overall experience; without creating glaring clashes between its new additions and legacy elements that, in some instances, are now over two decades old. And while there's still plenty I haven't seen after 78 hours and 35 levels, I can speak to one truth: WoW Forever is stunning work.

Perhaps it's best to start with WoW: Forever's most obvious changes: its new lighting and weather effects. People love to speak about getting lost in MMOs, being consumed by their digital worlds, but as much as I've enjoyed World of Warcraft in the past, its ageing graphics tech never managed to ensnare me that way. Forever's new visual elements, though, have gone a long way toward pulling me in.

highlights.title: Police told Russell Brand to leave Jemima Goldsmith's house in 2014
highlights.summary: Police confirm they asked Brand to leave his ex-girlfriend's house after she reported an alleged assault.
body: Police have confirmed they told Russell Brand to leave his ex-girlfriend Jemima Goldsmith's house in 2014 after she claimed a violent incident took place.
Thames Valley Police said officers were contacted by an alleged victim and went to an address in Oxfordshire on 25 July 2014 but no arrests were made.
They listened to her concerns and gave support, and "also ensured the victim's partner left the address, as per the victim's wishes", the police added in a statement on Wednesday.
Goldsmith, who dated Brand for about a year, wrote on X on Monday that she "had to call the police to have him removed from my house in 2014 during a violent incident" but chose not to press charges.

highlights.title: AI has made it ‘close to impossible’ to assess university coursework, regulator says
highlights.summary: Office for Students says institutions in England should return to traditional exams and in-person presentations. Universities should go back to traditional exams and in-person presentations to grade students after lecturers complained that AI has made it “close to impossible” to assess coursework…
body: The Office for Students (OfS) said the credibility of degrees from England’s universities was under threat from the prolific use of AI in essays, dissertations and “open book” exams, with students reporting that their peers boasted of using AI undetected by staff.

The regulator warned universities and other higher education institutions that failing to design “valid and reliable measures of students’ knowledge and skills” to combat AI could breach their conditions of registration and lead to sanctions being imposed.

Josh Fleming, the director of strategy and delivery at the OfS, said AI use in higher education “presents a generational risk to the system as it stands, threatening to undermine students’ learning and institutions’ ability to assess them”.
Fleming added: “We need to see far greater efforts to tackle these risks, including far greater use of AI-free assessment.

highlights.summary: ChatGPT is going to let you chat with verified "Business Agents" that represent a brand to help you with things like comparison shopping. The feature, available first to "eligible" e-commerce and online service businesses in the US, is launching as part of a suite of business-focused features in…
body: ChatGPT’s new AI agents represent companies and can help with things like comparison shopping.

You can start talking with a Business Agent if a business that has created one appears in a response from ChatGPT. While chatting with a custom agent, you can ask about a business’s offerings and ask follow-up questions, like asking about differences between two different products. Businesses can specify a Business Agent’s instructions and provide business context so that the agent knows how to respond.

Chats with Business Agents will be clearly labeled and separate from your main ChatGPT conversation, OpenAI says. To help people know that they’re talking with an agent that actually represents the business, companies will be able to claim their organization and get verified through a feature called Business Hub. (OpenAI isn’t sharing specifics about its verification methods because there are different methods for different businesses, VP of monetization Benji Shomair said in a press briefing.) Business Hub will also let companies see insights such as mentions in ChatGPT responses and top “discovery topics” where their business pops up.

But despite sitting out last weekend’s warm-up match at the Waca, early fitness work on tour has seen Bethell report swelling in the same knee. Scan results have been sent back to his specialist in the UK and his tour is now officially over.

A bystander at training on Wednesday, Bethell will travel home this weekend and undergo further assessment on a worrying issue that has kept him out of action since the third ODI against India at Lord’s back in July.

highlights.title: In One Scene, Prime Video Officially Rewrites Gandalf’s Mission in Lord of the Rings
highlights.summary: By the end of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season 2, Gandalf (Daniel Weyman) had chosen his name and wizard staff and found a mentor in the enigmatic Tom Bombadil (Rory Kinnear).
body: Tolkien’s wizards aren’t just old men who wield magical power. They are Maiar, primordial spirits who serve the Valar, the divine beings that helped Eru Ilúvatar create the world. Sauron is a fallen Maia who served the rebel Vala Morgoth. The five Istari are Maiar sent in the form of old Men to Middle-earth to stop Sauron. They became known as wizards, and their members include Gandalf, Saruman, and Radagast.

Those are the only three wizards mentioned by name in The Lord of the Rings, but Tolkien’s Unfinished Tales mentions there were two more who were sent to the East: Pallando and Alatar. In season 3, episode 3, it’s revealed that the Dark Wizard is Pallando. He wanted more than to serve the Valar, so he killed Alatar, an act so evil it turned Rhûn into a desert. Pallando clearly has regrets as he’s trying to regrow the Tears of the Valar lilies that used to cover Rhûn. He hopes that he can make the land green again using one of Sauron’s rings.

highlights.title: Mini record player on track for No 1 in Christmas toy parade
highlights.summary: Industry experts pick out tiny turntable as one of their ‘15 hottest toys’ for the festive season. A record player so small it belongs at a party in a Barbie Dreamhouse is one of this year’s must-have Christmas gifts as the vinyl revival takes an unexpected turn.
body: The £19.99 micro music set plays dinky 1.5in records and comes with an exclusive “mini vinyl” of the school disco favourite APT by Rosé and Bruno Mars. The toy makes the Toy Retailers Association’s annual DreamToys list of the 15 “hottest toys” this festive season.

The Mini Brands record player taps into the huge market for collectible toys. Part of the appeal is the 45 mini records to collect, ranging from Billie Eilish’s Birds of a Feather to Neil Diamond’s Sweet Caroline. The discs are sold separately in £8 “blind balls” with part of the attraction being the mystery of which songs are inside.

The trend for miniature products comes because making something smaller “makes it feel cuter”, suggests Melissa Symonds, executive director of UK toys at market research company Circana. While adults enjoyed the novelty, she suggested that children would relish acting out playing records in the same way that their parents did.

The record player is unlikely to satisfy high-end audiophiles, however, because the “vinyl” isn’t real. Instead, the discs contain a chip that activates a 30-second clip from the player’s internal memory.

highlights.title: Nintendo Defends Decision to Cut Mario and Yoshi Easter Eggs From The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake
highlights.summary: Nintendo has defended its decision to scrub the secret appearance of Mario characters from its The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake. Hidden away inside Hyrule Castle, the game's original 1998 version included a wall of portraits that featured Mario, Luigi, Peach, Bowser, and Yoshi artwork…
body: Visit the same area in Nintendo's newly-launched Switch 2 version, however, and all references to the Mushroom Kingdom have been removed. On a similar note, a selection of Zelda: Twilight Princess artwork has also been cut, having been snuck in when Ocarina of Time was re-released on 3DS.
Now, Nintendo has addressed its choice to remove these Easter eggs — and said that what was once a more "carefree" approach within Nintendo to referencing other games has been reconsidered.

"Certainly, at the time, when we put those there, I don't think anybody thought it was too big a deal," legendary Zelda series producer Eiji Aonuma told Game Informer. "Maybe there was a more carefree or comfortable approach to that sort of thing.

"But looking at it now... given the overall way that we're creating this world and giving the player that form of expression, if they look up and they think, 'Why is Yoshi there?' We don't want that moment to interrupt their experience of the world in that way. So we're feeling a little bit differently about it this time."

highlights.summary: We asked three stylish people in or adjacent to the fashion industry to chronicle one month of their fashion consumption—and to note what was purchased at full price, discounted, and gifted.
body: Welcome to Show Us the Receipts, our recurring column on what fashion people really buy and spend.

Money remains taboo in almost every corner of life, but in fashion, dollars and cents can take on an especially complex dimension—from both inside and out. With a high buy-in to the luxury market and wages that don’t often allow professionals access to the goods offered by their own industry, we often find ourselves wondering how, exactly, our contemporaries afford their wardrobes. Do they come from generational wealth? Are they on every PR gifting list known to man? Are they savvy sale shoppers and bargain hunters? Or are they just really shrewd budgeters?
This month, a corporate employee at a luxury house, a stylist, and a content creator all offered Vogue a peek at their receipts.

Giannis Antetokounmpo contributed a team-high 30 points to go with 11 rebounds and 4 assists, with Davion Mitchell of the Heat adding an additional 19 points (5-13 FG, 3-7 3P) in the game.
Darryn Peterson finished with a team-high 25 points along with 4 rebounds for the Jazz in the losing effort.
The Heat improve their record to 5-6 with the win, while the Jazz fall to 1-10 for the season.
